unit.why: A short anecdote told by R. Hayyim Vital about the Ari, who deliberately walked behind a scholar to honour him. It is copied from Sha'ar ha-Gilgulim / Shivhei ha-Ari (ש״ה ח״ב) and is not about a Hasidic figure.

stories.start_quote: פ״א היתי מהלך בדרך עם מורי
stories.summary_en: While walking with R. Hayyim Vital, the Ari kept walking behind a Torah scholar who had deliberately walked ahead of him, unaware of the Ari's stature. Asked why, the Ari explained that since the scholar took honour from it, he was obliged to honour him, as Hillel had run before Ben Tovia.

tags.why: Praise of the Ari's piety, from an older kabbalistic source
Placed in a chapter on honour (מענין כבוד) as a lesson in honouring scholars

quotes: היה תמיד ללכת אחריו אף אחר שהת"ח הלך לצד אחר
tags.why: The Ari humbles himself before a lesser scholar

quotes: היה הוא מחויב לחלוק לו כבוד ולעשות רצונו בכך
tags.why: The virtue of honouring Torah scholars
The scholar seeks honour by walking ahead
The disciple worries the Ari is violating the prohibition of placing a stumbling block

quotes: כי גם זה בכלל כבוד ת"ח
tags.why: The behaviour is justified by the law of honouring scholars and by Hillel's precedent
Dialogue between master and disciple, though they are kabbalists rather than Hasidim
